http_semantics.note: An operation on a non-existent resource (and on syntactically-hostile-but-legal names) is answered with HTTP 200 'ok'; the not-found outcome is signaled only by the business-level boolean result:false inside the success envelope, with no HTTP-level error status at all. The name-validation face does use HTTP 422 for structurally illegal names (NUL, overlong), so the disposition split is: structurally-invalid name -> 422; legal-but-nonexistent name -> 200+result:false.

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: DELETE on an existing collection returns HTTP 200; DELETE on a non-existent collection returns 404, not 200
contract_grounding.note: Violates-as-written is coherent: the quoted expected_behavior (contract assertions[8].expected_behavior, quoted verbatim also by the script's [assertion quote] line) contains an explicit status claim ('returns 404, not 200') and the in-chain primary observation (200 + result:false on a never-created name) directly contradicts it; the observed parameter (a syntactically-legal collection name) is inside the assertion's domain (any non-existent collection). Caveat for the auditor: the 404 clause itself is unsubstantiated by the cited documentation (see doc_verification and chain_trace) - the API violates the contract, but the contract over-claims relative to the doc. Note also: candidates.jsonl constraint_id field was empty; the id was recovered from the attack string, the script header (constraint_ids), and structured_contract.json assertions[8].

chain_trace.break_detail: The contract->doc link fails on content: the cited v1.18.x documentation page does not contain the assertion's 'non-existent collection returns 404' clause (page shows only the 200 response; the repo's own OpenAPI declares no 404-specific response for delete_collection). The doc_quote stored in endpoint_registry ('Deleting an existing collection is confirmed with 200; a non-existent collection returns 404.') matches the page only on its first half. The behavior link (script->log) is intact and the observed behavior is real and stable across scripts - but the DEFECT verdict rests on an assertion clause the documentation does not make (extraction over-claim), so downstream adjudication must weigh the contract as the sole normative source for the 404 requirement.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST face: actix delete_collection [Path<CollectionPath> validated: length 1-255 + validate_collection_name_legacy (rejects only '/' and NUL)] -> dispatcher.submit_collection_meta_op(CollectionMetaOperations::DeleteCollection) -> toc::delete_collection -> collections.write().await.remove(name) returns None for a never-created name -> else-branch sets result=false -> Ok(false) -> helpers::process_response -> HttpResponse::Ok().json({result:false,status:'ok'}) = the observed 200. gRPC face: tonic Collections::delete -> validate(request) -> perform_operation -> the SAME submit_collection_meta_op/toc path -> Ok(CollectionOperationResponse{result:false}) - both interface faces share the behavior (REST behaviorally observed; gRPC disposition source-traced, not exercised in the sandbox). Name-validation face (actix-web-validator -> validation_error_handler -> 422) explains why nul-percent00 and overlong-1000 were rejected while the legal-charset hostile names sailed through to the phantom 200. OpenAPI chain: openapi-collections.ytt.yaml delete: -> response(type('boolean')) -> 200(result:boolean) + generic 4XX + default; no 404 is declared for the missing-collection condition anywhere.
source_grounding.outcome_detail: With respect to the contract's required behavior (404 on a non-existent collection), the source contains no enforcing code: the delete path raises no NotFound error for a missing collection and returns Ok(false), which the HTTP layer maps to 200. The name-validation face DOES exist and works (structurally illegal names -> 422), which is why the NUL and overlong probes conformed. by_design_in_source is NOT available: the only comment in the missing-collection branch ('we hold the collection_create lock to make sure no one is creating this collection...') addresses locking, not the status contract; no code comment, docstring, or test pins the return-false-instead-of-404 behavior as intended (grep for delete/non-existent/idempotent intents found hits only in unrelated modules - resharding/quantization), and per the v3.4 tightening an unannotated silent behavior must not be marked by_design.

mundane_explanation.surviving: Two non-mutually-exclusive explanations survive for the auditor: (1) contract-extraction over-claim - the 404 clause may never have been a real documentation promise, in which case the API is schema-conformant with its own spec (result:boolean under 200) and the 'defect' is in the contract, not the vendor; (2) unannotated idempotent-delete design - the vendor's 200-with-boolean schema semantically accommodates result:false for a no-op delete, suggesting intended behavior, but the source carries no explicit by-design declaration, so this remains an inference rather than a recorded by_design_in_source.
